name: acpype-tool
description: ACPYPE 2026.9.5 for small-molecule topology generation and conversion of existing AMBER topologies to GROMACS. Includes Linux AmberTools and Open Babel. Python code environment packaged for PSC. Reads mounted inputs at /app/inputs and writes topology files and logs to /work.

code_environments.description:
Python 3.12 code environment with ACPYPE 2026.9.5, Open Babel, and
bundled AmberTools (antechamber, parmchk2, tleap, sqm, and charmmgen).
Runs on Linux AMD64 CPUs; no GPU or MPI required.

Available modules:
- acpype: ACPYPE topology generation and AMBER-to-GROMACS conversion
- openbabel: Molecular file conversion and SMILES handling
- subprocess: Run acpype and bundled AmberTools commands
- pathlib, shutil, glob: File management and result packaging
- json, re: Result serialization and parsing

Can handle:
- Ligand topology generation from MOL2, PDB, MDL/MOL, and SMILES
- AM1-BCC or gas-phase charge assignment with an explicit net charge
- GAFF/GAFF2 or AMBER atom typing
- AMBER, GROMACS, CNS/XPLOR, and CHARMM topology output
- Existing AMBER prmtop/inpcrd conversion to GROMACS
- Python workflow scripting, logging, and result packaging

IMPORTANT PATHS:
- /app/inputs: Input molecule and topology files mounted read-only
- /work: Writable working directory and output directory captured by Discovery

When invoking this Python code environment, set outputMounts to ["/work"].
The launcher runs the script in /work and records stdout and stderr in
/work/logs.out. Keep the script working directory at /work, or use a child
folder under /work, so ACPYPE writes its topology folders into captured output.
Use Path.cwd() or Path('/work') for output paths. Use absolute input paths.
The runner supplies scriptName; outputMounts specifies directories to capture
when execution finishes. Execute ACPYPE with subprocess.run and check=True.
The launcher preserves the Python script's exit status.

Python example for a neutral ligand:
  import subprocess
  subprocess.run(["acpype", "-i", "/app/inputs/ligand.mol2", "-b", "LIG",
                  "-n", "0", "-c", "bcc", "-a", "gaff2"], check=True)

Generate ligand topology with GAFF2 and AM1-BCC charges:
  acpype -i /app/inputs/ligand.mol2 -b LIG -n 0 -c bcc -a gaff2
Set -n to the molecule's actual integral net charge.
This creates LIG.acpype inside /work with AMBER, GROMACS,
CNS/XPLOR, and CHARMM files.
Use -o gmx if only GROMACS output is needed.

Convert existing AMBER topology and coordinates to GROMACS:
  acpype -p /app/inputs/system.prmtop -x /app/inputs/system.inpcrd -b SYSTEM

SMILES input is also supported:
  acpype -i 'CCO' -b ETH -n 0 -c bcc -a gaff2

Commands: acpype --help; acpype --version; obabel; python3; bash.
OMP_NUM_THREADS defaults to 1; keep thread use within the allocated CPUs.
Use topology files only with compatible AMBER/GAFF force fields.
